title: How Basie sets the tempo and why tempos creep up
summary: Greene says Basie sets tempo by the audience; today many pieces are played too fast.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: When Basie sets up the tempo in front of a number, how exact is he in his tempo tonight and the next night? Is that almost identical, or is it a matter somewhat of how he feels? I mean is one night a little faster, or is it pretty constant?
It depends on how he feels.
It does?
And, I think -- Basie does alot of things according to the audience.
Oh, he does, huh?
Yeah. He'll look out there and see what's happening. See what kind of audience it is.
See? That's just the same as Ellington, you know?
Yeah.
I mean, it's amazing. There's a second sense, isn't there?

Yeah, he'll check what's going on out there, and then he'll set the tempo, more or less. And, sometime it varies. Sometime he might -- later years -- he's inconsistent, more or less, as far as tempo is concerned. But, whatever tempo he finds -- that'll be it. We'll stomp it off in that tempo.

Yeah. Well, you know, Duke was criticized often because some of the things over the years -- the tempo went up, you know -- where he was playing it at what we would say was a bad tempo. Over a period of years it got faster and faster. And one of those was a thing he called 'Ke Ke' -- and critics were very severe about this because he played it faster. I asked him -- he said 'Well, the guys are bored with it. They like to play it faster'.
Well, that could be true.
It could?

You see, that could be true. You get new breeds, and they don't want to tolerate the slow things like tempo wise -- like we do, you know. I mean, there's alot of things we play faster now than we did. And it's a shame that we do, because it loses, to me -- it loses some of the dynamics, -- some of the feeling.
It's not what belongs.
Like, in the beginning, you know, like when you first start something out --
Well, it doesn't swing as much.

No. You see, to me -- you can get so much out of it. I don't know whether they realize that or not. You know, whether they want to tolerate that -- you know, you get in one groove and you're supposed to stay there, you know what I mean? Why not -- whatever groove -- get in it -- enjoy it. Don't try to get someplace else with it. You see, they're always trying to move ahead. You know, what's the sense of playing if you -- you know -- if you don't play it and enjoy it where it is? Instead of moving on -- trying to, you know, you play like you're trying to get it over with. You see?
Yeah. Distorted?
Yeah.
You mean sort of pushing?
Yeah. Pushing it so you can get it -- it makes it sound like you don't want to tolerate it. You want to get it over with, you know what I mean?
In other words, you're not talking of rushing the tempo, you mean you -- yeah. I can understand that.
You see what I mean? Playing it -- and if you stomp it off in one tempo -- okay -- play it in that tempo and enjoy it right there, you see?
